newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares ease after Yeltsin operation ends.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares ease after Yeltsin operation ends.

text.p: Russian shares lost some early gains on Tuesday after doctors and officials said heart surgery on President Boris Yeltsin had ended successfully.
Dealers said prices firmed initially on news the operation was over, but then fell back.
"Many people were speculating and waiting, many people made their bets... Now they have a lot of paper and many people have decided to take profits," said a Credit Suisse (Moscow) dealer.
"But the market is pretty balanced, with offers still meeting good demand."

Prices started to rise sharply when the market opened on news the operation on Yeltsin had started. Russian news agencies quoted a Kremlin spokesman as saying it had ended successfully at 2 p.m. (1100 GMT).
UES was quoted at 1250 GMT at $0.0844, off an early high of $0.0856, but up on Monday's $0.0830 close. LUKoil was at $10.19 after closing at $10.20 and hitting an early $10.40.
But dealers said the market could pick up tomorrow when foreign investors have digested the significance of the news.

"In the end this was an important event. Tomorrow there may well be a major rise in prices because positive rather than negative conclusions will be drawn," said, Renaissance Capital dealer Oleg Tatkov.
But even a successful outcome to the operation would not necessarily be enough to bring investors back into the market.
"This operation won't clear up all the problems," Tatkov said. "There are still problems with paying the IMF tranche, problems with tax arrears, and so on."
